concerns.text: The plan states that GPSW will be applied by fitting a Gaussian linear model of Recommendation_Diversity on Baseline_Vector and using the inverse conditional density as weights, but it does not specify how the continuous density will be estimated, how positivity will be checked, or how extreme weights will be trimmed beyond a simple >10× median rule. Without a clear density‑estimation strategy, the propensity scores may be misspecified, threatening causal‑independent balance.

No formal a priori power analysis is provided; the only safeguard is a GLS fallback when N < 30. This leaves the study vulnerable to type‑II error on realistic sample sizes (e.g., tens of thousands) because the detectable effect size is unknown.

Baseline_Interest_Vector is derived from pre‑study history but the dimensionality of this vector is not limited or regularized. High‑dimensional covariates can cause over‑fitting in the propensity model and inflate variance, yet no dimensionality‑reduction or regularization strategy is described.

Shannon entropy is used as the diversity metric, but entropy is confounded with list length (longer recommendation lists naturally have higher entropy). The plan does not describe any control for list length or alternative diversity measures, raising construct‑validity concerns.

The residual permutation test shuffles residuals while keeping the original predictors. This approach assumes exchangeability of residuals, which may be violated if there is heteroskedasticity or clustering by user. No justification or diagnostic for this assumption is provided.

Semantic merging of categories uses a single cosine‑distance threshold, but the impact of merging on the entropy calculation is only examined via a sensitivity sweep over thresholds {0.01, 0.05, 0.1}. No sensitivity to the choice of embedding model or to the merging algorithm itself is explored, leaving a potential hidden confound.
